newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs complacent about Senate election-survey.
newsitem.headline: Czechs complacent about Senate election-survey.

text.p: Voter turnout is likely to be low when the Czech Republic's first senate election is held on November 15 and 16, a public opinion poll published on Thursday showed.

The survey carried out in early October by the state-funded research agency IVVM showed 57 percent of 1,365 potential voters surveyed expected to cast a ballot in the first round of the election and only 52 percent said they would vote in a runoff planned a week later on November 23 and 24.
It also found that 46 percent of citizens did not know whether or not an election campaign was actually under way.
"There is, in general, low interest in the elections and the willingness to vote is low," Eliska Rendlova, an analyst at IVVM told Reuters. "A part of the public even rejects having the Senate."
A previous IVVM poll showed that 53 percent of Czechs harbour doubts about the necessity of a second chamber.

The elections will be the first for the newly created 81-seat upper house of parliament which will have limited legislative power, acting primarily as an advisory body to the lower house, the Chamber of Deputies.

Voter turnout in lower house elections in June was 76.41 percent, although surveys prior to that vote had suggested more than 80 percent planned to vote. In the end, the centre-left lost its overall majority in the chamber.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) and the leading opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) are the leading contenders in the Senate election.
